blocks.text: We have already seen that linear momentum plays an important role in translational motion of bodies. Similarly, another quantity known as angular momentum has important role in the study of rotational motion.
A particle is said to possess an angular momentum about a reference axis if it so moves that its angular position changes relative to that reference axis.
blocks.title: Angular momentum

blocks.text: The angular momentum L of a particle of mass m moving with velocity v and momentum p (Fig. 3.16) relative to the origin O is defined as:

blocks.alt: From the origin O a magenta arrow r reaches a particle of mass m. From m a blue arrow p points up and to the right at angle θ to the dashed extension of r. The line of p is extended backwards as a dashed line, and the dashed perpendicular from O to it is marked r sin θ.
blocks.caption: Figure 3.16 (the second figure with this number): angular momentum L = r x p of a particle about O (original drawing after the textbook's figure).
blocks.long_description: The book prints the number Fig. 3.16 twice, once for the rigid body in topic 3.4 and again for this figure.

where r is the position vector of the particle at that instant relative to the origin O. Angular momentum is a vector quantity. Its magnitude is:

blocks.text_alt: L = rp sinθ = m rv sinθ

blocks.text: where θ is the angle between r and p. The direction of L is perpendicular to the plane formed by r and p and its sense is given by the right hand rule of vector product. SI unit of angular momentum is kg m² s⁻¹ or J s.

blocks.text: The sphere in (a) is rotating in the sense given by the gold arrow. Its angular velocity and angular momentum are taken to be upward along the rotational axis, as shown by the right-hand rule in (b).

blocks.text: Now consider a symmetric rigid body rotating about a fixed axis through the centre of mass as shown in Fig 3.17. Each particle of the rigid body rotates about the same axis in a circle with an angular velocity ω. The magnitude of the angular momentum of the particle of mass mᵢ is mᵢvᵢrᵢ about the origin O. The direction of Lᵢ is the same as that of ω. Since vᵢ = rᵢω, the angular momentum of the ith particle is mᵢrᵢ²ω. Summing this over all particles gives the total angular momentum of the rigid body.
where I is the moment of inertia of the rigid body about the axis of rotation.

blocks.title: Example 3.5
blocks.problem: The mass of Earth is 6.00 × 10²⁴ kg. The distance r from Earth to the Sun is 1.50 × 10¹¹ m. As seen from the direction of the North Star, the Earth revolves counter-clockwise around the Sun. Determine the orbital angular momentum of the Earth about the Sun, assuming that it traverses a circular orbit about the Sun once a year (3.16 × 10⁷ s).
steps: To find the Earth's orbital angular momentum, we must first know its orbital speed from the given data. When the Earth moves around a circle of radius r, it travels a distance of 2πr in one year, its orbital speed vₒ is thus, vₒ = 2πr/t
Orbital angular momentum of the Earth = Lₒ = mvₒr
blocks.answer: The sign is positive because the revolution is counter clockwise.
